w: One of Croatia's oldest national parks, founded in 1949 in the karst mountains on the border with Bosnia and Herzegovina. UNESCO inscribed it in 1979 for its cascading tufa lakes, caves and interlinked waterfalls. The protected area covers nearly 297 square kilometres, mostly within Lika-Senj County.
s: Terraced tufa lakes and waterfalls since 1949

w: Named for a fighter against the Ottomans, preserved only in legend -- no one named Barac remains in the region. Opened in 1892, abandoned after World War II, reopened in July 2004. In 2022, tools likely made by Neanderthals turned up inside, next to a bear tooth and finger bone.
s: Reopened show caves hiding Neanderthal tools
